title: A neutral mean does not prove stable return
environment: Offline motion-analysis controls. No live body-motion acceptance or universal threshold choice was established.
goal: Decide whether a sampled motion window has returned to neutral.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Mean proximity, plus stability in a different window, was treated as sufficient.
what_worked: Historical correction: Require both mean-return proximity and return dispersion within the existing allowance, including selected and opposite-side joints; retain independent invariant failures. Verification reported by the source: Symmetric plus/minus translation and rotation fixtures now remained unverified rather than passing. Neutral and small-noise controls still passed. The recorded current run covered 128 related tests, not a new full-suite result.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Opposite displacements or rotations canceled to a neutral average while oscillation continued, yet the result was accepted.
why: Confirmed: return-window dispersion was computed but omitted from the acceptance decision.
improved_method: Validate central tendency and stability in every required acceptance window. Include adversarial cancellation fixtures instead of relying only on average error.
when_to_use: Offline motion-analysis controls. No live body-motion acceptance or universal threshold choice was established.
when_not_to_use: Do not extrapolate outside the recorded conditions or use partial evidence to claim general product or release acceptance.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
